title: The Hidden Danger of Overlooking These 5 Questions: Loss of Employee Commitment
author: Kurt Mueller
summary: Kurt Mueller argues that leaders lose employee commitment when they neglect a handful of simple questions in one-on-ones. He lists five: what resources the person needs, what obstacles hinder them, which working relationships are critical, what their next career interests are, and how the leader can better support them. A short coaching vignette shows a new manager acting on the answers by arranging training, buying software and fixing a cross-department communication gap. The case is that good questions plus real listening supply the information a leader needs to decide well and build trust.
points: Asking the right questions builds the trust and transparency that engagement and development depend on.
The five questions cover resources, obstacles, key working relationships, career aspirations and how the leader can better support the person.
Acting on the answers, as in the Sarah example, produced better training, tools and cross-department collaboration and raised morale.
Neglecting these questions leads to misinformed decisions and stalls employee growth.
Leaders must be willing to hear negative feedback as part of their own growth.
quotes: Why are these questions so vital, you might ask? Well, they establish a culture of trust and transparency, laying the groundwork for enhanced employee engagement and development. Gaining trust is paramount.
Question One "What resources or support do you need to excel in your role?" Providing the necessary tools is like empowering your employee to achieve their best work.
Question Two "What obstacles or challenges are hindering your performance?" It's akin to identifying roadblocks in a project; you need to know what's impeding progress.
Question Four "What are your interests for your next career step?" Aligning aspirations with the team's and your goals can foster a commitment to capabilities growth.
Neglecting these questions could lead to misinformed decisions and hinder the professional growth of your employees. Avoid that pitfall by implementing effective questioning techniques.
It's natural to feel apprehensive about receiving negative feedback, but it's a crucial part of your growth as a leader. Embrace it, learn from it, and watch yourself evolve into a remarkable leader.

Great leadership isn't just about making the right decisions; it's about ensuring you have the right information to make those decisions. So, go ahead, ask these questions, and witness your team reaching new heights of success.
